text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc said it was launching an analytical product that can be used to evaluate credit risks individually or across an entire portfolio.
The product, called CreditMetrics, will create an industry benchmark to quantify risks, J.P.Morgan said.

J.P. Morgan said CreditMetrics will enable a company to have an integrated view of credit risk across its entire organization and product spectrum. It will also provide indicators of value at risk due to changes in credit quality caused by upgrades, downgrades, and defaults, as well as portfolio concentration.

J.P Morgan said the product measures credit risk across a range of instruments, including traditional loans, commitments and letters of credit, fixed income instruments, commercial contracts including trade credits and receivables, and swaps, forwards, and other derivatives.
J.P. Morgan said the product does not calculate credit ratings or prices, but instead provides a tool to help managers improve their credit risk management decisions.

The product consists of three main components, J.P. Morgan said. One is a methodology for assessing portfolio value at risk caused by changes in credit quality. A second is an historical dataset available on the Internet. Third is a software package called CreditManager which implements the methodology of CreditMetrics.

Blythe Masters, head of J.P. Morgan's Global Credit Derivatives group, said in a statement the product provides a framework to evaluatee credit derivative and other credit transactions for hedging or investment.
